strategy_updates.pricing_theme: Pricing AI features and a new compute/storage-split Atlas offering on top of a consumption business
strategy_updates.current_model: Atlas is consumption-priced (cluster tier and hours, storage, data transfer; free, flex and dedicated tiers). The Atlas Infinite public preview (AWS only) bills compute separately, from $0.088/hr per HA shard for M10 to $5.417/hr for M60 Gen2, plus storage at $0.30 per GB-month on uncompressed data. The existing product is renamed Atlas Core (M10 dedicated $0.08/hr with storage included). Enterprise Advanced is a self-managed subscription.
posting_evidence: New US requisition: Pricing & Monetization Associate, New York (about 3 days a week in office), US base $84,000–$165,000, first published 2026-11-10, req 4273616033; the Toronto twin (JOB-0003) is inactive.
Sits in a dedicated Pricing and Packaging department and team; individual contributor, described as a Senior Analyst with 2–5 years in strategy, business operations or financial analysis.
Mandate: price and package new launches and changes to existing offerings, using historical customer data and trade-off analysis; build revenue, margin, cohort and usage models.
Works with Engineering on infrastructure costs and architecture to turn them into unit economics and pricing models; drives SKU, billing, selling and tooling execution.
Requires confident SQL (Python a plus); 90-day plan ends with scoping and launching a first major business case.

news.summary: MongoDB opened Atlas Infinite in public preview on AWS: compute billed separately from $0.088/hr (M10) to $5.417/hr (M60 Gen2), storage at $0.30 per GB-month, 24-hour continuous backup included; the existing product was renamed Atlas Core.
news.source: UsagePricing (tracking MongoDB pricing page and billing docs)

strategy_updates.interpretation: MongoDB is moving parts of Atlas from bundled cluster pricing to separate compute and storage meters (Atlas Infinite), while also pricing AI retrieval features. Both need cost-to-serve-based unit economics, and the posting asks for exactly that. Inference: rehiring the role in New York after the Toronto posting lapsed, inside a named Pricing and Packaging team, suggests the team is staffing up to model migration between Atlas Core and Infinite and to set SKUs before Infinite leaves preview. For a candidate, the work is likely heavy on usage and cohort modelling, which matches the SQL requirement, rather than headline list-price setting.
open_questions: Will Atlas Infinite replace Atlas Core pricing for new customers at general availability, and how will existing commits migrate?
Does the role own pricing for AI features (embeddings, reranking, MCP server) or only core Atlas SKUs?
Who leads the Pricing and Packaging team, and does it report into Product or Finance?
strategy_updates.caveat: Atlas Infinite prices come from a third-party tracker of MongoDB's pages, and the preview may change. The link between the role and Infinite is inference; the posting names no products beyond Atlas boilerplate.
